items.desc: Club bangers, high-concept artist albums, all night long sessions and wide-ranging DJ mixes - UK talent Leon Vynehall can do it all. More than just a producer, he is a thinker who likes to explore beyond the usual limits: in the past, he's served up novellas and short films to complement his music. His most recent album, 2025's In Daytona Yellow, centred around human voices and embraced real vulnerability. This week's mix takes a similarly thoughtful approach. It was, he says, assembled like an album with an underlying musical narrative loosely themed around 'humanity'. In between the selecti…
items.title: Dekmantel Mix 519 - Leon Vynehall

items.desc: Toronto's Ciel has never stuck to one sound, but what she plays is united by "various shades of dub-influenced electronic music." That is true of Slowburn, the party dedicated to slow chuggers that she has run since 2021, but also the music she's released on plenty of influential labels and the sets she plays across the world. The tempos, the timbre and texture might change as she traverses dreamy downtempo, wiggly tech house or psychedelic techno, but the warmth and sense of atmospheric pressure never do. This week's mix is about representing all of that in one ambitious two-hour trip, inclu…
items.title: Dekmantel Mix 518 - Ciel

items.title: Young Marco at Lotus - Lentekabinet 2026

items.desc: New Delhi-raised, Bali-based DITA steps up to our podcast series with a mix of wonderfully loose and elastic rhythms drawn from her own unique colleciton. There's a steamy tropical heat to everything, from the dubby grooves to the electro-tinged breaks, breezy house and 90s rave throwbacks, all mixed with great control. It's a colourful glimpse into DITA's world in 2026, full of new finds and old favourites that reflect years of musical influences. The mix arrives as DITA's international profile continues to grow, having established herself as a resident at Potato Head Beach Club in Bali. Her…
items.title: Dekmantel Mix 517 - DITA

items.desc: Amsterdam-based Hervé's endless curiosity for finding and sharing music takes him into all sorts of interesting in-between worlds. Groove and subtle progression, psychedelic swirls and deep bass are ever-present no matter where he heads, including Lentekabinet last year. As a producer, he keeps things layered and introverted, and beyond the decks he co-runs a label, event space and creative agency that help the scene to thrive. This week's mix was recorded at home in one take, on a sunny Saturday morning, and reflects the records Hervé has carried this summer while "channelling the energy tha…
items.title: Dekmantel Mix 516 - Hervé

items.desc: Now Amsterdam-based, Naone was shaped in her native South Korea. Her bottomless knowledge of 90s and 00s house and techno informs the sets she plays, particularly at the No Clubs events she is closely associated with. Beyond that, she heads up the Down2Earth label and expresses herself with productions that fuse ambient textures, acid lines and dubbed-out rhythms. Dekmantel Selectors is a few days away and to get you to the starting line, Naone has dropped 90 minutes of trippy tech house. From wiggy mind-melters to shadowy chuggers and dubby rollers, it's pure heads down dancing material that…
items.title: Dekmantel Mix 515 - Naone

items.desc: Dasha Rush emerged more than two decades ago but has never settled into one style. From techno sets on the main stage to more intricate experimentalism in the back room via floor-focused 12"s and a soothing ambient full-length, this self-confessed "hyperactive and neurotic" mind continues to ask questions of herself and her audiences. This weekend the FullPanda label head links with Oscar Mulero to close down the UFO stage at Dekmantel, so a mind-altering trip surely awaits anyone in attendance. As a taster before that main course, Rush has served up an hour of what she calls 'cerebral techno…
items.title: Dekmantel Mix 514 - Dasha Rush

items.desc: DJs have always had to dig for records, but Nicolas Lutz has taken the search for sound to obsessive new levels. The Uruguayan has spent more than 20 years excavating tunes, labels and artists most of us never knew existed. Genre is largely irrelevant; instead, the My Own Jupiter boss threads his finds into beautifully dark and alluring soundscapes full of mystery and tension. Playing in that way requires great technical skill as well as refined taste, and this week's podcast is further proof that Lutz has both in high supply. For almost two hours here, he navigates stark and moody atmosphere…
items.title: Dekmantel Mix 513 - Nicolas Lutz

items.desc: Ryan Elliott has been woven into the fabric of the underground for two decades. The Detroit native and Faith Beat label head cut his teeth back home before relocating to Berlin in 2009, where he became a core member of the Berghain and Ostgut Ton family that helped shape the sound of the contemporary scene. He has always straddled the house and techno divide, merging moods and rhythms from each into his own immersive soundscapes. Not long after a 12-hour, all-vinyl set at Berghain to mark his 50th birthday, Elliott has now selected an hour of "old, new, rare and unreleased music" and rolled i…
items.title: Dekmantel Mix 512 - Ryan Elliott

items.desc: Techno heavyweights Function and Nastia Reigel first came together over a shared love of early, rave-leaning and transcendental grooves. After months swapping tunes from both the old and the new school, they got to work in the studio and, in May, dropped their Devocion EP on Dekmantel. The four tracker explores broody and melancholic techno that is doused in emotion with plenty of shadowy atmosphere and deep rolling rhythms. Off the back of that, they have now put together a mix that explores this world even further with tracks from the likes of Donato Dozzy and Regis, plus two from their own…
items.title: Dekmantel Mix 511 - Function & Nastia Reigel

items.desc: Guy Blanken has been part of the Dekmantel family for almost 20 years. Under his Makam alias, he explores a light, deep and dreamy sound that contrasts with his darker work as Talismann. He recently returned to our label with the delightfully dubby house album Tarp, featuring tracks from the last 10 years, made all over the world with complete freedom. “It’s more about creating a space or a feeling than telling a specific story,” he told us recently. This July, Guy joins us in the woods for The Archive, a brand-new live show featuring plenty of treasures from his vaults. But first comes this …
items.title: Dekmantel Mix 510 - Makam

items.desc: Curaçao-born sound curator Rozaly both ignites and unites the dance floor. The sounds he plays are designed to blow open preconceptions about Caribbean music and tap into a more collective sense of memory. The distillation of his musical heritage through a new contemporary lens has made him a favourite at our festivals, which is why he will join us again in Amsterdam and Croatia this summer. But first, his mix, which he describes as "a dream through the night of the Caribbean" that starts in the evening and takes you through to early morning and touches on niche styles like zess, chutney and …
items.title: Dekmantel Mix 509 - Rozaly

items.desc: BASHKKA plays with a purpose beyond making people dance. The Munich-born artist is an advocate for the social and political power of electronic music and is a proud advocate of queer culture. Next to her residency at Amsterdam's Raum and Blitz Club in her hometown of Munich, she plays across the world while dropping evocative originals and remixes across the house spectrum. For this week's mix, she homes in on a seductive groove that is grounded in her own "sensual, hypnotic and driving" house music DNA. Technically mixed but full of selection flair, it's infused with glimpses of her own fort…
items.title: Dekmantel Mix 508 - BASHKKA

items.desc: Alfred Anders is the sort of character every good local scene needs—collector, curator, connector, risk-taker. This week, we get a taste of his mix, cruising at 110 BPM on the slower fringes of club music. A journey through trippy, outer-space spacelines and wonderfully weird grooves, moving from early ’80s house and tribal vibes to New Beat and Proto-Techno, all anchored by his Belgian sound as a guiding red thread. Behind the decks, he is one of the main arteries of the Brussels music scene and nightscape, digging deep for unknown gems that move, entrance, and intrigue. In 10 years time he …
items.title: Dekmantel Mix 507 - Alfred Anders

items.desc: Locked into the rhythm of today’s techno landscape, Berlin-based sorcerer Jesse G shapes an intense, ritualistic musical journey. This mix brings you to the depths of dark minimalism, melting into deep, psychedelic passages that become pacy and percussive before the boosters kick in and the trip gets cosmic. Her textures contain power, but never at the expense of emotional nuance, as elements of bass music, breakbeat and UK sound seep into her selections. Witness this Tresor Resident and Hard Wax staffer casting a seamless spell of punching grooves with psychedelic atmospheres at Dekmantel Se…
items.title: Dekmantel Mix 506 - Jesse G

items.desc: Hailing from Düsseldorf, Time Passages label head Binh takes crate-digging dedication to another level. His ear for discovering unknown gems has made him a long-time underground favourite, often showcasing his wax during marathon-length sets in Berlin or back-to-backs with fellow cult vinyl heads. Dive into 75 minutes of his signature minimal pressure: thudding kicks and spangled synths, laced with a dark yet futuristic mood. A taste of what’s to come when Binh joins us for the 10th edition of Dekmantel Selectors on the Adriatic coast.
items.title: Dekmantel Mix 505 - Binh

items.desc: Léa Occhi is Berlin-based, Paris-rooted, but hard-wired into the dancefloor’s more introspective frequencies. The co-founder and resident of queer collective Spectrum Waves channels techno into mental, minimal rituals that are emotionally charged and deep, regardless of energy levels. Outside of the club, she's a proud champion of marginalised communities who uses music to bring people together, despite being a reserved character herself. Ahead of her appearance at Dekmantel Festival 2026, Occhi soundtracks a world where tension, groove and inward reflection collide. Supple, deeply rooted rhy…
items.title: Dekmantel Mix 504 - Lea Occhi

items.desc: Amsterdam’s T.NO delivers the 503rd Dekmantel mix, giving a taste of what he’s bringing to this year’s festival season. The Rinse FM resident draws on his Surinamese heritage to weave kawina rhythms into club music with a sharp, contemporary edge. Bass-led and grounded in Afro-diasporic traditions, his productions carry a restless, exploratory energy on labels like TraTraTrax, Club Djembe and re:lax. His mix for us is a widescreen two-and-a-half-hour selection that dives deep into all aspects of his sound. After a serene ambient start, T.NO wastes no time in getting down to business and lays …
items.title: Dekmantel Mix 503 - T.NO

items.desc: Our first mix of the New Year is an otherworldly back-to-back between DJ Nobu & Aurora Halal that was recorded live at Dekmantel Festival 2023. Japan's Nobu is a renowned selector with a singular but fluid approach to techno and experimental electronic music. He’s the cult figure behind the long‑running Future Terror party series and Bitta label, both of which showcase truly adventurous sounds. Halal, meanwhile, is the Brooklyn‑based favourite who runs the respected Mutual Dreaming series and has a shadowy, psychedelic style that melts genres together with experimental textures. The pair repr…
